Folks — forwarding Helios' note (below). They want either a temporary measurement-window adjustment for APAC or an automated downgrade path to a lower-latency model variant. They asked for a plan by EOD tomorrow.

My take: we can offer a short-lived, documented "dynamic window carveout" that treats sustained bursts as a transient event (sliding-window-based carveout) for up to 7 days while they throttle/finish the campaign. Alternatively, we can push traffic for APAC to the quantized variant (faster p95) for the burst window. Both have tradeoffs: the carveout keeps model quality consistent but changes SLO accounting; variant routing preserves SLOs but may change output characteristics.

Please see the attached quick analysis (p50p95_analysis.csv) — I pulled a 24h slice and a few simulated rolling-window aggregates.

Can you do:
- Karthik: validate if we can implement a regional, route-level sliding-window carveout that triggers when sustained traffic exceeds X qps for >Y minutes (suggested X=1200, Y=10). Include rollback play.
- Markus: ops impact and billing/metric implications (how to annotate the carveout in our SLOs and dashboard).
- Connor: legal/procurement check — will Helios accept a documented temporary SLO accounting change + signed approval?

I want to keep Helios on the platform; we should propose both options with pros/cons and recommend one.

— Lauren

Lauren — quick technical view.

We can implement two patterns with minimal infra changes:
1) Sliding-window carveout: increase p95 measurement to use a 60-minute sliding aggregation for APAC for the affected route(s) and mark any contiguous window where qps > 1200 for > 10 minutes as a transient burst; those windows are annotated and excluded from monthly p95 billing SLO computation. Implementation: config change in routing + a tagging flag in the metrics ingestion pipeline. Risk: SLO visibility is altered; customers see an annotation but the absolute p95 number reported will differ from production behavior.

2) Model-variant routing: route APAC traffic to the quantized Llama-2-13B-q4 variant during the burst. Pros: p95 drops immediately; Cons: potential quality delta. Rollback trivial.

Operational notes:
- We should run the carveout as a feature-flagged rollout for 24 hours in staging, then enable for Helios with a 24h cooldown and a scripted revert.
- Add an automated alert if p95 remains > target after 72h post-change (to trigger CS + Sales escalation).

I'll draft the exact config diff by EOD.

— Karthik

Tom —

Thanks for the sample. After internal review we can offer two paths and propose the following recommended plan:

Recommended (short-term, lowest product disruption): enable regional model-variant routing for APAC on the impacted route(s) for a 72-hour window. This keeps p95 within target while we monitor output quality. If after 72 hours the p95 is stable, we will either revert traffic back to the higher-quality variant or keep routing with your sign-off.

Alternative (SLO-accounting approach): implement a documented "sliding-window carveout" that annotates and excludes contiguous high-qps windows from p95 computation for up to 7 days, with explicit start/end times and signed approval. This preserves model output but changes reporting and billing SLOs.

Action items we need from Helios by EOD PT tomorrow:
- Which option do you prefer (variant routing or measurement carveout)?
- If carveout, confirm the start time and maximum duration (we recommend max 7 days).
- If variant routing, confirm acceptance of potential minor output deltas and whether you want a fallback to the original model after 72 hours unless you request an extension.

I've attached a short MOP in Drive for review: https://drive.google.com/open?id=1a2b3c-proposed-mop.

If you prefer, we can spin up a 30-minute sync tomorrow morning to finalize.
